name: 3DO Interactive Multiplayer
description: A CD-based console standard from Trip Hawkins' The 3DO Company, licensed to manufacturers such as Panasonic, Sanyo and GoldStar rather than built in-house. Launched in 1993, it was one of the first 32-bit CD consoles and showcased full-motion video and early 3D, but its high price kept it niche.
curiosities: The Panasonic FZ-1 launched in the US at $699.
The core hardware was designed by Dave Needle and RJ Mical, who had earlier worked on the Amiga and Atari Lynx.
3DO's planned successor, the M2, was sold to Matsushita (Panasonic) and never released as a home console.
Each licensed manufacturer had to make a profit on the hardware itself, since 3DO only earned royalties on software.
